history.summary: Lyndenwoods is CapitaLand's 343-unit 99yr new launch at Science Park Drive (D05, TOP ~2029) — the first Science Park residential project in 40 years. This 4BR at $3.435M / $2659 PSF sits at the very top of the project's range (URA median $2583) and at $3.4M absolute on a leasehold tenure, exit liquidity is the binding constraint.
history.rating_rationale: $2659 PSF is above even the project's own median of $2583 — you're paying top-of-stack for a new-launch 4BR — and $3.435M absolute on a 99yr lease pushes well past the liquid band; CCR freehold becomes a direct competitor at that price. The 342-txn count reflects launch sell-down, and the rate carries new-launch bias (inflated developer pricing). Score 436/1000 despite a respectable Elo. Reputable developer (CapitaLand) and One-North/Science Park employment are real positives, but a $3.4M leasehold 4BR bought above project median has little appreciation headroom and a thin resale pool.
red_flags: $2659 PSF above project URA median ($2583) — paying top-of-stack
$3.435M absolute on 99yr lease — competes with CCR freehold, thin buyer pool
New-launch bias in the rate (developer pricing inflation)
TOP ~2029 — construction/market risk before any exit window opens
catalysts: First Science Park residential in 40 years — scarcity narrative
650m to Kent Ridge MRT; One-North/NUS/Science Park employment catchment

agent_evaluation.rental_assessment: Tenant demand from Science Park/One-North/NUS is strong, but a $3.4M 4BR is family-let with a shallow pool and a sub-3% gross yield at this PSF — weak income relative to outlay.
agent_evaluation.appreciation_assessment: Limited headroom: bought above the project's own median PSF at full new-launch pricing on a leasehold tenure, much of the upside is pre-paid. Do not override the new-launch-biased rate upward.
